enumeration_note: One taught skeleton: fade a liquidity sweep at an untapped HTF S/R level on a lower timeframe with wick/engulfing/exhaustion confirmation, stop beyond the swept level, target 1:2. Timeframe (5m/1m), single-rejection vs double-bottom second-touch confirmation are compatible variants of the one skeleton â€” grouped, not split. The 'trap' (wick-above-resistance-short / wick-below-support-long) is the same fade logic applied symmetrically at resistance vs support, not opposing logic.

coaching_notes: find where the obvious trades are sitting, and do the opposite
look for clean price action that's just a little too clean â€” equal highs, trend lines, or zones that look perfect â€” that's the bait
anticipate where price is going, not react to it
always keep an eye out for the traps
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: on daily/4h chart, mark most recent swing highs/lows and clean S/R levels that haven't been tapped yet (where liquidity lives)
ENTRY: wait for price on the 5m/1m to rapidly approach and tap a marked HTF liquidity zone
ENTRY TRIGGER: rejection wick at the zone
ENTRY TRIGGER (alt): bullish or bearish engulfing candle
ENTRY TRIGGER (alt): exhaustion candle / long wick
ENTRY TRIGGER (alt): volume spike or volume divergence at the tap
TRAP/FADE DIRECTION: price wicks above resistance then dumps -> short; price wicks below support then reverses -> long
STOP: below the swept level / below the current London low
SELECTION: do not enter before price taps the liquidity zone; wait for confirmation
FILTER: trade around London or New York open sessions (when most stop hunts happen)
FILTER: do not chase breakouts; only fade trapped moves
SECOND-TOUCH VARIANT: on second rejection of same area with bar not closing beyond the level, take a double-bottom reversal for 1:2
strategies.entry_summary: Mark untapped higher-time-frame (daily/4h) swing highs/lows and clean support/resistance levels. Drop to the 5-minute (or 1-minute) chart and wait for price to rapidly approach and tap one of those zones with a volume spike; enter on the rejection â€” a rejection wick, bullish/bearish engulfing candle, exhaustion candle, or volume divergence. Fade the sweep: go long when price wicks below support and reverses, go short when price wicks above resistance and dumps.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop below the swept level (worked example: below the current London low); target a fixed 1:2 risk-to-reward.
strategies.name: ltf_liquidity_sweep_rejection_scalp
